items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1993-07-17
items.q: I remember once, I sent him a bill. In fact, it was a Fats Domino session.

ctx.x: You know? He was sometimes downright mean-spirited with people. Even me. I remember once, I sent him a bill. In fact, it was a Fats Domino session. In those days, the early days, I was only charging $15 an hour for the studio. Fifteen? The studio and me, both, okay? Fifteen bucks an hour. And I sent the bill, and he sent me back a letter, without using those words, saying I overcharged him. And he said things like, well, there are studios out here that make yours sound like crap and all that. And I only paid $35…
Wow. Yeah. Well, anyone else come to mind from the early days?

items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1994-01-15
items.q: He only invested his friendship and his relationship with people if they meant something to him otherwise in business. That was my experience with him.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. What about his relationship with Lou Chud?

Well, Chud, from what I can tell, didn't invest a lot of personal capital into anybody. I don't mean dollars and cents. I mean relationship capital. Mm-hmm. And I think that even with his enormous support over a long time of Dave Bartholomew, it was all bottom line oriented. Mm-hmm. I may be oversimplifying Lou Chud's personality. But if I had to oversimplify it, I would say it was that. He only invested his friendship and his relationship with people if they meant something to him otherwise in business. That was…
